figures.shows: The worked example of the clamp on one brightness axis: eight pixels at 0.1 and a glint at 1.0, the range clamp from 0.1 to 1.0 that keeps a history of 1.0, and the variance box up to 0.554 that pulls it there
figures.caption: The worked example on one brightness axis. The range clamp reaches the glint, so a history of 1.0 stays; the variance box ends at 0.554, and the clip pulls the history down to it.
figures.alt: A brightness axis from 0 to 1.0. Eight pixels sit at 0.1 and one glint at 1.0. A blue bar from 0.1 to 1.0 keeps an orange history dot at 1.0. A green bar from 0.1 to 0.554 ends where an orange arrow brings the history from 1.0.
figures.numbers: The page's worked example: mean 0.2, deviation about 0.283, Clip Width 1.25 (Sharp), box top 0.554, box bottom the range's 0.1 (TAA.comp.slang lines 111 and 112 limit the box to the range).

figures.shows: The same moment of the Showcase's fourth camera flight, over the grain of the wet apron, drawn with the Original and Sharp presets, cropped to the ground near the camera
figures.caption: The same moment of the camera's flight over the apron. Original blurs the grain of the ground, and Sharp keeps it crisper: its resampling term and the sharpening of the shown image both keep detail.
figures.alt: Two crops of the same rough ground, brown on the left and golden toward the sun on the right, seen from a moving camera. In the first the grain is soft and blurred. In the second the grain has sharp, dark edges.

figures.blocked: At the pin the take shows no trail to compare: in the fourth flight at step 600 the range clamp and variance clipping differ only in the fine noise of the apron and in a halo around the sun, and no crop of the frame shows a faint copy beside a glint that one removes and the other keeps (2026-11-24, three takes agreeing).
figures.shows: The Showcase's fourth camera shot in flight, around a glint, with the range clamp and with variance clipping
figures.caption: Where the moving view carries a dark edge past bright glints, the range clamp leaves a faint copy beside the glints, and variance clipping removes most of it.
figures.alt: Two crops of the same moving view around bright glints. The first has a faint trail beside the bright spots. The second has almost none.

figures.blocked: At the pin the clamp already removes the ghost of the falling crate: rejection off and on differ in 169 pixels by at most 5 levels, because the brown crate and the pale bricks and sky it uncovers differ in colour (2026-11-24, three takes agreeing). The case the paragraph names, a dark object leaving a dark wall, needs matching materials that no sample places.
figures.noStandIn: The code, the numbers and the flowchart of the disocclusion test that follow the paragraph teach the test fully, and a picture of the pin would show no ghost to remove.
figures.shows: A wooden crate falling in front of the Physics Playground's north brick wall, with disocclusion rejection off and on
figures.caption: With rejection off, the wall that the falling crate uncovers keeps a ghost of the crate for some frames. With it on, the wall is clean at once.
figures.alt: Two crops of a brick wall behind a falling crate. The first shows a pale ghost of the crate on the wall above it. The second shows a clean wall.

figures.blocked: At the pin the clamp already removes the drag of the Ghost boxes: with Transparent Weight 0 and 0.5 the falling boxes differ only in a line of pixels along their edges, which no reader sees, because the plain pale boxes fall outside the colours of the bricks and the sky around them (2026-11-24, three takes agreeing). A textured blended surface moving over a still background would show the drag; no sample holds one.
figures.noStandIn: The paragraph states the reactive mask rule and its coverage in full, and a picture of the pin would show no drag to remove.
figures.shows: The Physics Playground's see-through ghost boxes falling into the pit in front of the brick wall, with Transparent Weight 0 and 0.5
figures.caption: With no extra weight the falling see-through boxes drag their image behind them. With a half weight the drag is gone.
figures.alt: Two crops of see-through boxes falling in front of a brick wall. The first has a smeared copy above each box. The second shows the boxes cleanly.
